briefings.headline: Death Toll Hits 67 as Thousands Storm Spain's Ceuta Border
briefings.body: At least 67 people died in Spain's Ceuta border crisis with Morocco, including migrants who drowned and others killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier. Tens of thousands have since crossed back into Morocco following the mass border event at the Spanish enclave on the northern African coast.

sources.title: Death toll in Spain border crisis reaches 67 as tens of thousands cross back in to Morocco
Watch: Tens of thousands of migrants enter Spain's Ceuta from Morocco

briefings.why_it_matters: The crisis marks one of the deadliest border incidents in recent European history, intensifying pressure on Spain and the EU over migration policy and border security.

briefings.headline: Fed Proposes Modernized Limits on Loans to Bank Executives and Insiders
briefings.body: The Federal Reserve Board opened a public comment period on a proposal to update its rules governing credit extended to bank insiders — a category that includes executives, board members, and major shareholders with potential influence over a bank's lending decisions. The existing rule, which sets conditions and limits on such loans, would be modernized under the proposal. The Fed is soliciting feedback before finalizing any changes.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on a proposal to modernize its rule governing the extension of credit to bank "insiders"—bank executives, board members and major shareholders who could potentially influence a bank's lending decisions
Federal Reserve Board requests comment on a proposal to modernize rules for mutual banking organizations

briefings.why_it_matters: Updated insider lending rules could affect how banks manage conflicts of interest at the top, with direct implications for the safety of deposits held by everyday customers.

briefings.headline: Trump's Media Company Sells Early Access to His Posts for $100K a Month
briefings.body: Trump's media company is offering investors early access to the president's Truth Social posts for fees reaching $100,000 a month. Legal experts say the paid subscription service may violate insider trading laws, as Trump's posts frequently move markets and influence policy expectations. The tiered early-access program gives paying subscribers a window to act on the president's statements before they reach the general public.

sources.title: For sale: early access to Trump's Truth Social posts

briefings.why_it_matters: If the service violates insider trading laws, ordinary investors who lack $100,000-a-month access could be systematically disadvantaged every time the president posts market-moving content.

briefings.headline: Trump Administration Rolls Back Biden-Era Workplace Heat Protection Rules
briefings.body: The Trump administration is reversing steps taken by the Biden administration to protect workers from extreme heat on the job. Where Biden pursued formal safeguards against dangerous temperatures in the workplace, the Trump administration is adopting a more lenient posture toward employers. The policy shift leaves workers with fewer regulatory protections as heat-related workplace hazards grow.

sources.title: Trump Administration Is Undoing Plans to Boost Workplace Heat Protections

briefings.why_it_matters: Workers in physically demanding or outdoor jobs face greater risk of heat illness with weaker federal protections in place.

briefings.headline: Pennsylvania High School Stayed Silent After Boys Made AI Nudes of 59 Classmates
briefings.body: A Pennsylvania high school is defending its decision to stay silent after male students used AI to generate nude images of 59 female classmates. The school argues gaps in existing laws limit its obligation to act or notify victims. The case highlights how current statutes have not kept pace with AI-generated image abuse, leaving schools with unclear legal duties and students without guaranteed recourse.

sources.title: High school defends staying silent while boys made AI nudes of 59 classmates

briefings.why_it_matters: If your child's school faces a similar incident, existing laws may give administrators legal cover to say nothing — leaving victims and parents in the dark.

briefings.headline: Woman With Cancer Reflects on Life, Death, and Inner Strength
briefings.body: Karán Founds-Benton spoke with a friend for StoryCorps about her cancer diagnosis and what it means to face death. In the conversation, she reflected on her life and expressed a sense of personal resolve in confronting her illness. The StoryCorps recording captures her perspective on mortality and the emotional experience of living with a terminal diagnosis.

sources.title: 'I can do this': Woman with cancer reflects on her life and facing death

briefings.why_it_matters: Hearing one person's unfiltered account of facing a cancer diagnosis can help others navigating serious illness — or supporting someone who is — feel less alone.
